name: Delbacháem
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Delbacháem was an Irish goddess or heroine of the Otherworld. Her mother held her captive in a high tower. The mother was Coinchenn, a fierce warrior woman. A curse said Coinchenn would die if her daughter wed. Coinchenn beat every suitor in battle. Then Art mac Cuinn, king of Tara, took up the task. His stepmother, the fairy Bé Chuma, had placed him under a geis. He could not eat until he stole Delbacháem from her magical island. Art won the contest. He freed Delbacháem, and her mother died. He then banished Bé Chuma from Tara.
objective: This entry records Delbacháem, an Otherworld goddess or heroine held captive in a tower by her mother.
